text:
maya: Heads up — CI on master is red for `test_fastpath_serialize` (linux-gpu). Failing intermittently, 3/12 runs today. Logs show assertion in worker timer ordering.
sam: link to failing job? can you paste the CI URL? :eyes:
maya: https://ci.internal.redwood/gh/redwood/inference/12345 — failing step `runtime-tests (linux-gpu)`

maya: log snippet:
```
E   AssertionError: expected [A,B,C] got [A,C,B]
  File "runtime/worker/scheduler_test.py", line 214, in test_fastpath_serialize
    assert order == expected_order
```

john: hmm that looks like nondet ordering from the timer wheel. I saw something similar with the preemption patch last week. Could be scheduling jitter.
sam: can we just rerun the job a few times to confirm flakiness before a deep dive? I'll trigger a rerun.
ci-bot: @sam triggered rerun for job 12345 — build 12346 queued. :fast_forward:
sam: 3 quick reruns done — 1/3 failed, 2/3 passed. definitely flaky.
lina: if it's timer ordering, try forcing deterministic scheduling env: `RUNTIME_SCHED_DETERMINISTIC=1 pytest -k test_fastpath_serialize` — does it reproduce locally?
maya: running locally now with deterministic flag. if it passes locally, might be timing on GPU nodes.

maya: local run (deterministic) passed. ran 10x without failure.
john: okay that's telling. candidate causes: timer jitter due to high load, or missing lock in worker startup. Can someone bisect recent commits touching `worker/scheduler` or `fastpath`?
sam: started a bisect across `main~50..main` with our bisect tool: `./scripts/ci-bisect --test runtime/worker/scheduler_test.py::test_fastpath_serialize --range main~50..main` — will update when it finds a first bad.
ops-bot: Bisect job queued (bisect-789). Estimated runtime ~35m.
sam: bisect found first bad commit: `d3f4b1a - reduce-timer-quantum` (touches scheduler timing constants). suspect.
lina: interesting — that commit reduced the quantum from 10ms to 1ms to lower latency. Might expose ordering races. Can we revert locally to verify?
maya: checked out `d3f4b1a` locally, ran 50 iterations on CI-like hardware: 9/50 failed. on previous commit `d3f4b1a^` 0/50 failed. Revert confirms.
john: OK rollback candidate. We should either revert the change or add a small yield in the fastpath to avoid the race. Also add a test harness that seeds scheduling.
lina: proposal: revert the quantum change in main, open follow-up to reintroduce with proper synchronization. I'll draft PR.
sam: tagging @oncall and SRE to schedule a canary rollback on the GPU pool if CI persists in master.
ops-bot: Notified @oncall. Runbook: https://wiki/internal/runbooks/ci-rollback
maya: thanks all — I'll watch the revert PR and validate once merged. If anyone wants to take the follow-up, assign to john/lina.
sam: 👍 will keep monitoring.

maya: final note — adding flaky test label and a short reproduction snippet to the issue: `pytest runtime/worker/scheduler_test.py::test_fastpath_serialize -k 'fastpath' --runs 50`

john: good. thanks everyone. :rocket:
